findings.desc: Docs cite latest measured baseline/RSS values that do not match story evidence. performance-index doc lines 51-77 label full baseline as latest with 39,825/6,439/12,520/10,873 and RSS 1,504,083,968/3,294,199,808, but checklist evidence lines 62-64 records final full baseline as referenceFullScanMs=49347 indexedColdMs=6972 indexedWarmCacheMs=1 indexBuildMs=14132 warmPrimeMs=11270 and no evidence was found for those RSS values. entry-layer doc lines 24 and 26 also cite RSS 646,414,336 and 3,845,570,560 with no matching story evidence; performance evidence lines 465-467 records peakRssBytes=3610689536.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 85ce7f952: docs now label the metric tables as canonical checklist-bound evidence and use the reviewer/checklist values (baseline 49347/6972/1/indexBuild 14132/warmPrime 11270; performance 38547/6825/1/RSS 3610689536). Unbound later local spot-check values are removed from the docs, and the entry-layer doc says RSS is run-dependent instead of citing unmatched values.

findings.desc: Fuzzy overflow can silently break reference/full-scan parity. buildFuzzyTokenIndex caps each fuzzy needle at 4096 tokens and records overflowNeedles (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-index.ts:268-288), but rarestNeedleForToken returns overflow=true only when no bucket exists (lines 520-540). fuzzyTokensContaining then uses the capped bucket and reports fallback=false (lines 543-554), so matchingIds does not run scanMatchingIdsForToken and keeps tokenScanFallbacks at 0 (lines 586-599). The pre-optimization matcher scanned all token-map entries for indexedToken.includes(token) / token.includes(indexedToken) (main:packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-index.ts:393-403). This means any query whose selected n-gram bucket overflowed can miss valid full-scan matches while the performance proof still reports no fallback; tests appear to assert normal counters but do not cover fuzzyOverflowDevMemoryTokens or fuzzyOverflowPlaybookTokens overflow behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 6c4e7c0a4: overflowed fuzzy buckets are no longer trusted as complete membership proof; rarestNeedleForToken skips capped buckets and fuzzyTokensContaining falls back to token-map scan when every usable fuzzy needle overflowed. Added M2 regression in playbook-runtime-memory-index-smoke proving 4,120 overflowneedle rows still surface candidate mem-overflow-4119 with tokenScanFallbacks>0/tokenMapScannedEntries>0. Verified with build, index smoke, M3-M6 full smoke, performance full smoke, and baseline full smoke.

findings.desc: Caller-supplied runtimeIndexSourceDigests can turn a stale cached pack into a fresh-looking pack. BuildMemoryFreshnessPackOptions exports runtimeIndexSourceDigests (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory.ts:159-174), and resolveRuntimeIndexForPack accepts the runtimeIndex whenever that caller-supplied tuple equals the index manifest, without reading current sources (lines 613-624). On cache hit, getRuntimeMemoryPackCacheHit computes currentSourceDigests via sourceDigestsFor; when a runtimeIndex is present that function uses context.runtimeIndex.manifest.sourceDigests instead of readRuntimeMemorySourceDigests (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-memory-cache.ts:226-228, 426-436). Thus a caller holding an old runtimeIndex plus its manifest tuple can get stale relevant cache content returned as freshness.class=fresh before contribution refs are rechecked. The benchmark passes runtimeIndex.manifest.sourceDigests as this tuple (packages/main/src/core/playbook-runtime-baseline.ts:1449-1467), so the optimization is not bound to an independently current digest proof. This conflicts with the pack contract that freshness reflects current source digests at consumption time, even though authority remains non_authoritative/gateEvidence=false.
